calls.reason: The only evidence is a single Reuters report from Jan 31, 2024, where Microsoft and Alphabet fell on rising AI costs. That cuts against investor indifference, but one trading day can't settle market attitudes, and no generative-AI profit data is supplied.

The PYMNTS summary of WSJ reporting describes mixed reviews: some testers worried about mistakes, others found Copilot useful. Microsoft's earlier early-access survey was favourable. Neither shows customers in general disliking it.

The claim is a subjective, hedged judgement. Tech Brew's informal test found the ad's results took more effort than shown but were technically achievable, which neither confirms nor refutes 'outright lying'.
The linked Dropbox images could not be inspected, and no authenticated record of the author's session was found, so the personal observation can't be checked.

The main point holds: the FT reported Altman saying OpenAI was lossmaking and likely to need tens of billions more, and later reporting projected big losses until 2029. The $1.6B was a December run rate; actual 2023 revenue was about $1B.
